title: docs(skills): a user field's declared deleteBehavior is taught in the data skill's field-types and relationships rules

_Requested by **Irene** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TJXtQ1tVD26ecLDZxFS67x?thread=cmsg_01TJXtQ1tVD26ecLDZxFS67xRY2TwWjfFKsjhqoNR7z9DE)_

Fixes #29400

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:objectstack-data 技能的两份规则文件现在教「`user` 字段上作者写明的 `deleteBehavior` 在删除该用户时真的生效」:field-types 的 `user` 行列出 `deleteBehavior`(无默认;写了就按 lookup 的方式 cascade / set_null / restrict,没写则保留被删用户的 id);relationships 的 Delete Behaviors 节点名删除联动读 `lookup`、`tree`,以及只在声明了值时才读的 `user` 字段。加一条 eval 用例练它。
- 为什么改:PR #29368 已把该行为合入引擎(card #29253),其 `Skills-docs: follow-up` 行欠下本卡;技能文本此前只说 user 字段「存储同 lookup」,没说删除用户时会发生什么,AI 写元数据时会把 `deleteBehavior` 当摆设或漏写。
- 风险与回滚:纯技能文本与 eval 夹具,无代码、无契约改动。两个 token 天花板都就地付账(删掉在本包别处已有完整版本的 Summary 示例块与 When-to-Use 列表),上限行未动,无 re-wrap。回滚即 revert。
- 先看:`skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md` 新段(Delete Behaviors 节末)与被删的 When to Use 节;`skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md` 的 `user` 行与被删的 Summary (Roll-up) 块;`skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json` 的用例 6。
- 两分钟验证:`node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`,预期 field-types.md 3183/3207、relationships.md 3844/3873,全绿。
- 需要你做的:Tier H 受管面(`skills/**`),需要 `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` 的批准;PR 保持 draft。

## What changes

Facts are taken from current `main`, not the card text alone: `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx` as corrected by PR #29712, `statesDeleteSemantics` / `cascadeRelationBehavior` in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, and the pins in `packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-user-field.test.ts`.

1. **`skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md`, the `user` row.** The Key Config cell adds `deleteBehavior` (no default — declared, deleting the user acts as on `lookup`: `cascade` deletes the holders, `set_null` clears the field or drops that member, `restrict` refuses with `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED`; undeclared, the field keeps the deleted user's id). Everything else in the row is byte-identical.
2. **`skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md`, Delete Behaviors.** One new paragraph after the `master_detail` code block: the walk also reads `lookup` and `tree` (`set_null` by default — the field is cleared; a `multiple` field loses only that member — or an authored `cascade` / `restrict`), and a `user` field only when it declares a value: deleting the user then cascades, clears or refuses exactly as a `lookup` does; undeclared, the field keeps the deleted user's id. `restrict`, and `set_null` on a `required` field (a `multiple` one only when the removal would empty it), refuse the delete with `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` — the multi-valued narrowing is the engine's (`cascadeDeleteRelations` escalates unconditionally only for a single-valued field and otherwise refuses only the rows the removal would empty; pinned in `engine-cascade-delete.test.ts`). The existing `master_detail` text above it is byte-identical.
3. **`skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json`.** Case 6: a required `owner` user field that must block deleting a held user (`restrict`) and a multi-valued `watchers` field whose deleted member should simply drop out (`set_null`). Must-contain pins the two `deleteBehavior` values, `type: 'user'`, `multiple: true` and `required: true`; must-not-contain refuses `reference: 'user'` and `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'`. The eval README's index line names the `user` case ("`deleteBehavior`, on a `user` field too"). Eval fixtures are measured, not ratcheted.

### Token ratchet, paid in place (no ceiling row moved, no re-wrap)

| file | tokens before / after / ceiling | lines before / after |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `rules/field-types.md` | 3207 / 3183 / 3207 (headroom 0 → 24) | 264 / 250 |
| `rules/relationships.md` | 3869 / 3844 / 3873 (headroom 4 → 29) | 420 / 414 |
| `evals/objects-fields-relationships.json` (not ratcheted) | 1436 / 1749 | 101 / 120 |
| `evals/README.md` (not ratcheted) | 142 / 148 | 12 / 12 |
| package `skills/objectstack-data` (17 files) | 44130 / 44399 | 3971 / 3970 |

The two payments, each a deletion of text restated elsewhere, with its home:

- `field-types.md` → the **Summary (Roll-up)** block under Common Field Configurations (14 lines, 361 bytes). Home: `rules/relationships.md` → Roll-up Summaries carries the same `summaryOperations` block with the same keys and comments plus the `filter` / `relationshipField` teaching; the Calculated table row in field-types.md keeps the key shape (`{ object, field?, function, relationshipField?, filter? }`). The deleted block's own last comment pointed at `rules/relationships.md`.
- `relationships.md` → the **When to Use lookup vs master_detail** section (14 lines) and its link in the table of contents (613 bytes together). Home: the Relationship Types table directly above it (Lifecycle, Required, Use Case columns), the Incorrect vs Correct section (lookup vs master_detail on invoice line items), and the Patterns examples. Its one line not restated there — `set_null` is the `lookup` default — moves into the new Delete Behaviors paragraph. Its `task.assigned_to → user` example taught a `lookup` to a `user` object, which this package's own eval 2 forbids (`reference: 'user'` is must-not-contain; a `user` object does not exist), so that line was also stale.

The package grows by about 270 tokens: the eval fixture and its index +319 (not loaded into a customer session), the two loaded rule files −24 and −25. Their ceiling rows could be lowered to 3183 and 3844 in a follow-up; this card's file surface does not include `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`.

## Why

PR #29368 (card #29253) made a `user` field's declared `deleteBehavior` take effect when the user is deleted, and its `Skills-docs: follow-up` line owed this card. Before this change the data skill said only that a `user` field is "stored identically to `lookup`", and its Delete Behaviors section spoke of `master_detail` alone, so an AI authoring metadata from the skill had no way to know that `deleteBehavior` on a `user` field is now enforced, that it has no default, or that a `required` field's `set_null` refuses the delete.

## Tests

- `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`: exit 0 — `57 authored bundle file(s) within their ceilings`; `rules/field-types.md is 3183 tokens (ceiling 3207; headroom 24)`, `rules/relationships.md is 3844 tokens (ceiling 3873; headroom 29)`.
- The eval fixture re-serializes byte-identically for cases 1–5 (checked before appending case 6), and every `must_contain` string of case 6 appears in its `expected_output`.
- No code changed, so no package test, typecheck, ablation or dogfood battery is owed (`Clause-②: no`, no `!` in the title).

## Acceptance notes

- The edit is made on the branch the platform fixes for this thread (`claude/project-thread-5yjezo`) in this container's own checkout rather than in a sibling worktree: the branch can be checked out in one place only and the container is this card's alone. Noted as a deviation from the worktree-first spelling, not from its purpose.
- `master_detail` text in both files is left exactly as it was; the card asked for the `user` teaching only.
- The `lookup` row of field-types.md still lists `deleteBehavior` without its default; relationships.md now states the default once. Not expanded further (small feature, small text).
- Round 2 (commit 5039eb23) answers the seat's contract review of dceca372 (comment 6595584700): M1, the required + `set_null` sentence now carries the multi-valued qualifier; S1, the eval README index line reads as a sentence. Nothing else moved. `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx` carries the same unqualified sentence for a `user` field and is the docs lane's follow-up, not this PR's.

## Verification

Head `5039eb23` (two commits: dceca372 the change, 5039eb23 the review's M1 + S1). No code changed, so no package test or typecheck is owed; the derived gate set is the verification.

All 32 ran on each head in a tree with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` done and `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/objectql` built, each with a 900 s timeout, each exit code captured before any pipe.

Not a finding: this diff touches no `packages/**` file, and the gate's own text says nothing was measured. CI's `Lint & Repo Gates` run on the PR is its reading.
